title: BankrollTransaction
description: One cash-movement event in the canonical bankroll ledger (data/edgelab/bankroll/transactions.jsonl). Phase 1 scope: observability/tracking only -- this schema and lib/edgelab/bankroll.py never feed into staking size, Kelly sizing, or any production risk-gate decision (see scripts/risk_gate.py, which is deliberately untouched by this milestone). Only DEPOSIT/WITHDRAWAL/ADJUSTMENT/STARTING_BALANCE/USER_REPORTED_BALANCE are ever written directly; stake-reserved/stake-returned/realized-P&L exposure is always computed live from the PlacedBet ledger (see lib/edgelab/bankroll.py:compute_bankroll_summary), never stored as a separate transaction, so the two ledgers cannot drift apart.

type.description: STARTING_BALANCE: the one-time opening balance a bankroll history begins from. DEPOSIT/WITHDRAWAL: real cash movement into/out of the trading account. ADJUSTMENT: any other correction, always carrying a reason. USER_REPORTED_BALANCE: a manually-entered snapshot of the user's actual account balance, kept for reconciliation/comparison only -- never used to compute or override the ledger's own settledBankroll/availableBankroll (see bankroll.py's module docstring).

amount.description: Signed dollars. DEPOSIT/STARTING_BALANCE/ADJUSTMENT(positive) increase the ledger; WITHDRAWAL/ADJUSTMENT(negative) decrease it. For USER_REPORTED_BALANCE this is the reported absolute balance, not a delta.

occurredAt.description: When the transaction actually happened, ISO 8601 UTC (may differ from createdAt for a late-entered transaction).

reason.description: Required in practice for ADJUSTMENT (enforced by lib/edgelab/bankroll.py, not this schema) -- free-text explanation.

reference.description: Optional pointer to whatever prompted this transaction (e.g. an external transfer confirmation id). Never a betId -- bet-driven exposure/P&L is always computed, never stored as a transaction row.

enteredBy.description: Free-text identifier of who/what recorded this transaction (e.g. 'chat', 'github_form', a username).
